title: InitGen slice economizer: hedged fallback and fair tenant allocation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: Short interactive requests (single-turn chat replies, short completions) are sensitive to prefill latency. Current prefill/decode pipeline favors throughput for bulk workloads, which increases tail latency for low-token requests during high-utilization periods. Goal: introduce an InitGen Slice Economizer that dynamically chooses initgen slice sizes and kernel fallbacks to reduce median and tail latency for short requests while preserving aggregate throughput for long-running jobs. The feature combines: 1) attention-aware slice sizing (smaller slices for low-attn-density prompts), 2) a hedged fallback path that can run on a low-latency quantized kernel when queueing exceeds threshold, and 3) a tenant soft-credit allocator to maintain fairness across customers. Success metrics: 25-40ms median prefill latency improvement for <=32-token completions under mixed load, 95th percentile tail latency reduction of 15% without >5% throughput regression for long sequences. Implementation notes: - Add a lightweight attn-density estimator in the prefill admission stage (budgeted compute, <50us per request). - Attach kernel_hint metadata to requests and allow runtime to speculatively schedule a hedged task on a compatible quantized kernel. - Introduce tenant soft-credits that accrue when tenants are throttled; scheduler consumes credits to prevent starvation. - Expose a runtime flag and console dashboard (per-tenant) to tune hedging thresholds and slice-size caps. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime-1.19 flag; start with dark launch traffic (5% of requests) then gradual ramp (20% -> 50% -> 100%) while monitoring rollback signals. Backout: revert flag or lower hedging concurrency to zero. Risks: inaccurate attn estimator may mis-route and harm quality; hedging increases GPU work if not tuned; fairness model complexity may introduce oscillation between tenants. Mitigations: conservative defaults, bounded hedged concurrency, and per-tenant circuit-breaker. Testing: unit tests for estimator, integration test with synthetic mixed short/long workload, end-to-end canary with customer A/B groups, and quantitative regression checks integrated into CI (latency and throughput baselines).

notes: Implementation detail: prefer lightweight CPU estimator to avoid increasing GPU critical path. If estimator confidence < 0.6, fall back to baseline slice sizing.
Kernel selection: runtime will prefer full-precision kernel when quantized path alters softmax scale beyond 1e-3 for the first iteration; quantized hedged path used only as latency-first fallback.
Fairness policy: soft-credit accrual rate = 0.1 credits/sec when underutilized, spend rate = 1 credit per hedged-accept. Tuneable via console.
